request:
Preserve real Git errors for provenance push failures

## Problem

When remote provenance persistence fails, GitWeave currently discards the underlying Git diagnostic and replaces it with a generic message:

```text
Provenance push failed; local refs and notes retained for Git inspection and retry
```

The stated reason is that Git stderr might contain credentials.

This is a preemptive protection that makes real failures harder to diagnose. Users cannot directly tell whether the problem was authentication, a missing remote, a rejected ref update, transport failure, or another Git error.

GitWeave should begin from normal Git behavior and avoid hiding useful diagnostics unless a concrete leakage problem requires targeted redaction.

## Expected outcome

Preserve the underlying Git failure information for provenance push failures.

Do not replace every Git error with one generic persistence message merely because stderr could theoretically contain sensitive text.

Prefer normal Git diagnostics by default.

If a concrete credential-leak path is demonstrated, redact only the specific sensitive value or field responsible rather than discarding the complete diagnostic.

Local refs and notes should still remain available after a failed persistence attempt.

## Context

The guiding principle is:

> Do not remove observability to defend against a hypothetical failure mode.

The provenance layer should stay close to ordinary Git push semantics, including useful Git failure diagnostics.


User directive: GitWeave implements, creates a separate PR, reviews/fixes iteratively and merges only when clean. Stop on unsupported operations or permission/allowance limits and ask the user. No parent manual substitute is authorized.
